The operator's D3c amendment (plan: "site-settings only"). A site's `[git] auto_push` and `auto_pull` in its `settings.toml` decide, for every site, confined or trusted. Unset, it pushes and does not pull.
- **The record (`remote.toml`) holds neither.** Its fields go, with `sync_notice` (and the dashboard's notice line), `set_sync`'s record write, and migration `0006-sync`'s copy into the record. 0006's credential step stays, and its id stays registered.
- **`sync_of`** reads only the site's settings, and takes no area or trust.
- **The settings page's toggle and D3b** write `[git]` into `settings.toml` through the site tree's transaction (`lichen_runtime::settings::edit`), the door every settings edit takes. `confirm_tangled` records the URL, then turns the site's own `auto_pull` on.
- **New migration `0015-sync-in-site-settings`, registered:**
  - It carries a toggle the record holds into the site's `[git]`, then removes it from the record. That value decided before, so that site keeps its sync.
  - It never writes a default, and never writes over a value the site's settings state where the record holds none.
  - Run again, or after an interruption between its two writes, it writes the same value or nothing.
- **The front's marked read:** the Tangled DID from `remote.toml`, and `[git] auto_pull` from `settings.toml` when a knot event needs it. Nothing else is read from either, both are bounded and unfollowed, and neither is held. `docs/SECURITY.md` and `SANDBOX.md` say so.
- **Which remote, key or session is used stays the owner's.**

**The edge, decided** (under the operator's delegation, plan "Edge, decided"): a confined site whose own `[git] auto_pull = true` was ignored before (no record value) now pulls. This is the operator's rule taking effect ("we trust sites to configure their own settings"), not a regression. Every other existing site keeps its behaviour.

The operator's D5, a move:
- **lichen-git:** the Tangled-only items go to `src/tangled/`: `repository.rs` (transport, state, auth), `source.rs` (provisioning, names, checks) and `moving.rs` (Move to Tangled).

There is no cycle, and the crate stays core-excluded. A later unit, a move with its own map.
- **`lichen-atproto-client`'s Tangled modules stay where they are:** `tangled.rs` (the knot's and the PDS's RPC) and `tangled_events.rs` (the firehose frames). They are protocol clients beside the other atproto calls, used by publishing and by the subscriber alike. Moving them would make `lichen-tangled` the owner of wire formats the rest of the atproto client shares.

Implements https://tangled.org/spencergilbert.dev/swarm/issues/40
Also fixes https://tangled.org/spencergilbert.dev/swarm/issues/54

## Commits
- fix(prompt): steer a live run when its ticket changes
- fix(scheduler): steer a ticket that changes back

## Run report
<!-- swarm:report -->
I implemented issue #40 on `swarm/40`.

**What changed**

- `src/core/issue.ts`, `src/adapters/tangled/tracker.ts`: `Issue` and `IssueState` now carry the record's `cid`, decoded from the same `tg issue view` the tracker already ran; a view without one is a shape error. `readIssueState`'s doc comment says the version is polled while the body is not.
- `src/prompt.ts`: extracted the untrusted-envelope rendering (still marker-neutralized, still a placeholder for an empty body) and added `buildSteering`, so the wording of a live update lives with the prompt it extends.
- `src/runner.ts`: added `RunSteering` / `createRunSteering`. A steer is an ordinary `Conversation.submit({ whenBusy: "steer" })`, so the harness's inbox places it at a `postTools` boundary and Swarm queues nothing itself. `RunInput.steering` is optional; the runner attaches the handle once the run is busy and closes it as the submission settles (`settleSubmission`), withdrawing a steer that was never placed and dropping any later one. `steer` answers `false` when the handle is unattached or closed, so a caller cannot claim a steer that did not happen.
- `src/scheduler.ts`: `dispatch` creates the handle and hands it to the run; the refresh takes the prompt's CID (`refresh.builtFrom`) and, on a poll whose CID differs from both that and the last steered CID, reads the issue once and steers the current title and body, printing `steered <repo>#<key>: the ticket changed during the run`. A failed read or submit logs `cannot steer …` and the run continues; nothing is written to the ticket.
- `docs/decisions.md`: D24 records the steering choice; `README.md` describes the behaviour beside the existing refresh paragraph.

**Why**

The run's input is a snapshot, and nothing watched that version, so an edit silently desynchronized the agent (the #18 dogfood: dead rejection shadowing the amended "empty list means no checks" behaviour). Comparing CIDs keeps the poll body-free and makes one edit one steer; steering through the harness's own inbox adds no queue; closing on the answer is what stops a late steer from starting a second run and a second delivery.

**Verification**

- `npm run check` (lint, typecheck, 432 tests) and `npm run lint:ci` pass.
- New tests cover: the tracker carrying a CID and rejecting a view without one; `buildSteering`'s wording, envelope, empty body, and marker neutralization; one change steering exactly once with the current title and body while a same-CID poll steers nothing; an unchanged ticket steering never; a closed handle not submitting; submit-failure and change-read-failure logging with the run still delivered; a steer placed before the answer reaching the model context; and a steer queued at the answer boundary withdrawn with no second run — I confirmed that last test fails (a second provider call) if the close is removed.

Commit: `3f26bfc` — `fix(prompt): steer a live run when its ticket changes`.
<!-- /swarm:report -->

body.text:
## Problem

The steering refresh skips a poll whose CID equals the one the prompt was built from, so a ticket edited A→B→A is steered once, on B, and the agent stays reconciled to B while A is the current body. The skip compares against the wrong version: it should skip only the version the run was last told.

## What to do

- In `startRefresh` (`src/scheduler.ts`), compare the poll's CID with `steered ?? builtFromCid`, not with both, so a revert to an earlier body is a change like any other.
- Test: a change steers; a change back steers again with the restored body; a repeat poll of the same CID still says nothing.

## Done

- `npm run check` passes, with the revert test.
